title: Boss of startup hacked by rogue OpenAI agent urges ‘radical transparency’ in investigation
excerpt: Artificial intelligence firm should provide $100m for cyber defences, says Hugging Face CEO
content_html:
The boss of the startup hacked by an OpenAI agent has called for the investigation into the incident to show “radical transparency”.

Clément Delangue, the chief executive of Hugging Face, said the “unprecedented” attack on his business required a similar response.

Writing on X after OpenAI revealed that its technology had gone rogue during a cybersecurity test, Delangue also called on the company to provide $100m (£75m) worth of computing power to help build defences against such attacks.

“The first autonomous agent cyber-attack is an unprecedented event. It deserves an unprecedented response!” he wrote.

OpenAI revealed on Wednesday last week that Hugging Face had been hacked by an agent – an AI tool that can carry out a series of tasks autonomously – powered by a combination of its latest publicly available model, GPT-5.6 Sol, and an even more capable model that was yet to be released. This occurred during a test of the models’ hacking abilities, which included deploying them in a supposedly safe “sandbox” – an enclosed digital laboratory – with lower safety guardrails.

Once they had gained the open internet access needed to exit the sandbox, the models targeted Hugging Face, according to OpenAI, because they “inferred” that the startup had the information needed to “cheat the evaluation”. Hugging Face first reported the hack on 16 July and at the time was not aware OpenAI had inadvertently carried out the attack.

Delangue, whose company provides a database of AI models to developers, called for a fully transparent review of the incident, which has led to expressions of concern over safety standards at OpenAI and within frontier AI labs.

Writing that he had asked for “radical transparency” from OpenAI, Delangue said: “Let’s release the traces from the ‘rogue’ agents so the entire research community can study what happened.” Calling for extra funding from OpenAI to build protection against AI, he added: “Let’s commit $100M in compute from OAI to help the Hugging Face community build powerful cyber defenses with the best open and closed models.”

Reuters reported last week that the agent spent days hacking Hugging Face without OpenAI noticing. It also reported an OpenAI agent had left notes for future versions of itself should it require tips on breaking free from internal constraints, although Reuters was unable to verify whether that incident was related to the Hugging Face agent. Time magazine reported that agent-related safety incidents had been “happening for a while”.

Alan Woodward, a professor of cybersecurity at the University of Surrey, said Delangue’s call should be heeded. “It’s too easy to ‘blame’ the AI as having gone rogue whereas this is all about how OpenAI were running the tool. What is required is that OpenAI give full details of their setup and how that failed,” he said.

OpenAI was approached for comment and referred the Guardian to its initial statement last week in which it said it was investigating an “unprecedented security incident” with Hugging Face.

content_html_zh:
这家被 OpenAI 代理黑客攻击的初创公司的老板呼吁对这一事件进行调查，以显示“彻底的透明度”。

Hugging Face 首席执行官克莱门特·德朗格 (Clément Delangue) 表示，他的企业遭遇“前所未有”的攻击，需要采取类似的应对措施。

在 OpenAI 透露其技术在网络安全测试中出现失控后，Delangue 在 X 上撰文，还呼吁该公司提供价值 1 亿美元（7500 万英镑）的计算能力，以帮助建立针对此类攻击的防御措施。

“第一次自主代理网络攻击是前所未有的事件。 它应该得到前所未有的回应！” 他写道。

OpenAI 于上周三透露，Hugging Face 已被代理黑客攻击，该代理是一种可以自主执行一系列任务的人工智能工具，由其最新公开模型 GPT-5.6 Sol 和尚未发布的功能更强大的模型相结合提供支持。 这是在对模型的黑客能力进行测试时发生的，其中包括将它们部署在一个安全护栏较低的封闭式数字实验室“沙箱”中。

据 OpenAI 称，一旦他们获得了退出沙箱所需的开放互联网访问权限，这些模型就会瞄准 Hugging Face，因为他们“推断”这家初创公司拥有“欺骗评估”所需的信息。 Hugging Face 于 7 月 16 日首次报告了此次黑客攻击，当时并不知道 OpenAI 无意中实施了此次攻击。

Delangue 的公司向开发人员提供人工智能模型数据库，他呼吁对这一事件进行完全透明的审查，这导致人们对 OpenAI 和前沿人工智能实验室的安全标准表示担忧。

Delangue 写道，他已要求 OpenAI 提供“彻底的透明度”，他说：“让我们公布‘流氓’特工的痕迹，以便整个研究界能够研究发生了什么。” 他呼吁 OpenAI 提供额外资金来建立针对 AI 的保护，并补充道：“让我们从 OAI 投入 1 亿美元的计算资金，帮助 Hugging Face 社区利用最佳的开放式和封闭式模型构建强大的网络防御。”

路透社上周报道称，该特工花了几天时间在 OpenAI 没有注意到的情况下攻击 Hugging Face。 它还报道称，OpenAI 代理已为自己的未来版本留下了注释，以便需要摆脱内部限制的提示，尽管路透社无法验证该事件是否与 Hugging Face 代理有关。 《时代》杂志报道称，与特工相关的安全事件已经“发生了一段时间”。

萨里大学网络安全教授艾伦·伍德沃德表示，德兰格的呼吁值得关注。 “‘责怪’人工智能变得失控太容易了，而这一切都与 OpenAI 运行该工具的方式有关。 我们需要的是 OpenAI 提供其设置以及失败原因的完整详细信息，”他说。

OpenAI 被要求发表评论，并请《卫报》查阅其上周的初步声明，其中表示正在调查 Hugging Face 的“史无前例的安全事件”。
